Now write SiteOptions and adapt shared infrastructure.

Now the RichText (markdown subset) renderer.

Now modify NestService for persistence + tombstones, and update JS.

Now the global stylesheet.

Now the About page combining all three.

Now the xunit stub for compile verification.

Now new web tests for nest persistence and work helpers.

Now the Data integration tests.

Now container, compose, env, and scripts.

I've attached the whole repository as one tar.gz. Extract it next to your clone and everything lands under `myblazorplayground/`. It builds with no warnings even with warnings treated as errors, and all the tests pass, but I couldn't run it the way you will (see the last section).

**Running it next to MyRestaurant**
- `scripts/instance.sh up` builds the image, starts PostgreSQL and the site, opens a quick tunnel, and prints the URL and the setup code.
- It uses `127.0.0.1:8090` for the site and `127.0.0.1:5433` for PostgreSQL. MyRestaurant uses 8080, 8443 and 5432. Its compose project, volume, image and tunnel container (`myblazorplayground-tunnel`) all have their own names.
- The first run creates `.env` with a random database password. Keep that file, because the database volume is created with that password.
- `/setup` asks for a one-time code that the server writes to its log; `scripts/instance.sh setup-code` shows it. Since anyone can reach the tunnel URL, the code is what stops a stranger from making themselves administrator.
- `backup` and `restore` are a single `pg_dump`, because the sign-in keys are stored in the database too.

**What's in it**
- **Project tracker** (needs an account):
  - Projects with editors and members, a ranked backlog, sprints, a board, and stories, tasks, bugs and epics.
  - Each item keeps a change history.
  - Descriptions and comments use Markdown. You can paste or drop screenshots and files into them; they upload straight away and the link is inserted where the cursor is.
  - Files are stored in PostgreSQL in 1 MB pieces. The default limit is 95 MB because Cloudflare refuses uploads over 100 MB; you can change it in `.env`.
  - On a phone, the board columns swipe sideways and each card has a status menu. On a computer you can also drag cards between columns.
- **Homes** (the nest features): everything is now saved in PostgreSQL as well as in each browser. When an entry is deleted, connected browsers drop it too, and a browser that was offline can't bring it back.
- **Toys** (all the chaos features): ported unchanged. They still keep their data in memory only, since forgetting is part of the design.
- **Deleting:**
  - Anyone can edit, but only administrators and editors of that project or home can delete.
  - Deleted things go to a trash, and only administrators can delete for good.
  - Every deletion, restore and permanent deletion goes in the audit log, along with role changes, sign-ups and failed sign-ins.

**Decisions you may want to revisit**
- **Markdown, not HTML.** The site turns Markdown into HTML itself and never passes raw HTML through, so there's no third-party sanitizer to get wrong. Pasted formatted text is converted to Markdown in the browser.
- **Passwords use PBKDF2** (built into .NET) rather than Argon2 as in MyRestaurant, to avoid a dependency.
- **No passkeys**, because a quick tunnel's address changes and would orphan them.
- **PostgreSQL 18.** Version 19 is scheduled to go stable today (November 19). Moving to it means changing the image tag in `compose.yaml`, `scripts/test.sh` and the CI workflow, then dumping and restoring existing data.
- **No npm lockfile.** npm in my sandbox couldn't generate one, so `package.json` pins exact versions and the scripts use `npm install`. Commit the lockfile your first install creates.
- **`/read` shows a "no articles" notice** because `wwwroot/nytimes.txt` wasn't in the chaos dump. Copy it over from chaos.
- **Docs:** decision records are in `docs/adr`, including the chaos and nest ones that still apply.

**What I checked, and what I couldn't**
NuGet and the container registries were blocked here, so I compiled against stand-ins for Npgsql, Dapper and xUnit, the latter two backed by a real local PostgreSQL 16.
- 78 domain tests, 359 web tests (including all the ported chaos and nest ones), 14 database tests and 311 JavaScript tests pass.
- I ran the site in a browser through setup, a project, items, sprints, the board, comments, uploads and downloads, members, permissions, delete, restore, permanent delete and the audit log. That turned up three bugs, now fixed:
  - Default form values were getting lost.
  - The board scrolled sideways on phones.
  - Login keys were read before the database tables existed.
- **Not yet run:**
  - The real Npgsql and Dapper packages.
  - The live parts of the pages: homes sync, the toys, and paste or drag in the tracker. Blazor's own script wasn't available here, though the forms all work without it.
  - The container build.
  - The tunnel script.

Your first `scripts/test.sh` and `scripts/instance.sh up` will be the first real run of those.

# myblazorplayground — first delivery (2026-11-19)

Delivered as a full tar.gz (358 files). Layout: Domain / Data (Npgsql 10.0.3 + Dapper 2.1.89, own SQL migration runner) / Web (Work, Nest=homes, Chaos=toys, Identity, Administration).

Key decisions (see docs/adr in the repo):
- Ports 8090 (web) and 5433 (postgres), compose project `myblazorplayground`, tunnel container `myblazorplayground-tunnel`, so it sits next to MyRestaurant (8080/8443/5432).
- `scripts/instance.sh up` = containers + quick tunnel; `/setup` needs a one-time code from the log (`instance.sh setup-code`).
- Roles: admin (site), project editor/member, home page editors (`home:<key>`). Soft delete -> trash; admin-only hard delete; everything audited in the same transaction.
- Homes persist to `nest_entry`; deletions are tombstones sent as `deleted` ids to browsers. Toys stay in memory.
- Rich text = server-rendered Markdown subset; paste/drop uploads into 1 MiB `attachment_chunk` rows; 95 MiB default limit (Cloudflare 100 MB).
- PostgreSQL 18 in containers; PG 19 GA was scheduled for 2026-11-19 (one-line bump later).

Verification done in the sandbox: build with warnings-as-errors (.NET 11.0.100), domain 78 / web 359 / data 14 tests passing against real PostgreSQL via a psql-backed driver harness, 311 Vitest tests, and a Playwright run of setup -> project -> items -> sprint -> board -> comments -> upload/download -> members -> delete/restore/purge -> audit.
Not verified here: real Npgsql/Dapper packages, blazor.web.js interactive islands, the container build and the tunnel script (no NuGet or registry access in the sandbox).
